extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys, and USPTO officials
extracted.subtask_description: Statutory rules implementing administrative patent proceedings, preissuance third-party submissions, venue, fee-setting authority, entity-size fee reductions, fee schedules, and prioritized examination under U.S. law (Public Law provisions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Trial and Appeal Board (PTAB) composition and duties
rubrics_metrics.description: The administrative patent judges shall be persons of competent legal knowledge and scientific ability appointed by the Secretary, in consultation with the Director. The Patent Trial and Appeal Board shall review adverse decisions of examiners on patent applications (section 134(a)), review appeals of reexaminations (section 134(b)), conduct derivation proceedings (section 135), and conduct inter partes reviews and post-grant reviews (chapters 31 and 32).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any reference to Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences is deemed to refer to the Patent Trial and Appeal Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three‑member panels requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Each appeal, derivation proceeding, post-grant review, and inter partes review shall be heard by at least 3 members of the Patent Trial and Appeal Board, who shall be designated by the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only the Patent Trial and Appeal Board may grant rehearings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of prior appointments; de facto officer defense
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary of Commerce may deem appointments of administrative patent judges who previously held office under Director appointments to take effect as of the Director's original appointment date. It is a defense to a challenge to such an appointment that the judge was acting as a de facto officer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provision addresses continuity of prior appointments upon statutory change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals to the Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit and waiver of §145/§146 remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant dissatisfied with a final PTAB decision under section 134(a) may appeal to the United States Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit; filing such an appeal waives the right to proceed under section 145. A patent owner dissatisfied with a final reexamination decision under section 134(b) may appeal only to the Federal Circuit. Parties to inter partes or post-grant reviews dissatisfied with final written decisions under sections 318(a) or 328(a) may appeal only to the Federal Circuit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For derivation proceedings, an appeal to the Federal Circuit may be dismissed if an adverse party, within 20 days after the appellant files notice of appeal, files notice with the Director electing to have proceedings conducted under section 146; the appellant then has 30 days to file a civil action under section 146 or the Board's decision governs further proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director's role in appeals and intervention
rubrics_metrics.description: In ex parte appeals, the Director shall submit in writing to the court the grounds for the PTO decision addressing all issues raised. The Director has the right to intervene in appeals from PTAB decisions entered in derivation proceedings or in inter partes or post-grant reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amends section 143 to require the Director's written submission of grounds and affirmatively grants intervention rights in specified appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preissuance submissions by third parties — eligibility and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Any third party may submit for inclusion in the record of a patent application any patent, published patent application, or other printed publication of potential relevance to examination if the submission is made in writing before the earlier of (A) the date a notice of allowance is given/mailed, or (B) the later of (i) 6 months after the application is first published or (ii) the date of the first rejection under section 132 of any claim by the examiner during examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective upon expiration of the 1‑year period beginning on enactment; applies to applications filed before, on, or after that effective date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preissuance submissions — required content and fee
rubrics_metrics.description: A preissuance submission must (A) set forth a concise description of the asserted relevance of each submitted document, (B) be accompanied by such fee as the Director may prescribe, and (C) include a statement by the submitter affirming that the submission was made in compliance with the section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director may prescribe fee amount and procedural details by regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Venue for civil actions relating to patents and trademarks
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical amendments change statutory references to the 'United States District Court for the District of Columbia' to 'United States District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia' for listed sections (e.g., 32, 145, 146, 154(b)(4)(A), 293 of title 35 and 21(b)(4) of the Trademark Act).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to civil actions commenced on or after the enactment date (as specified).

rubrics_metrics.name: Director's fee‑setting authority and cost‑recovery limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may set or adjust by rule any fee established, authorized, or charged under title 35 or the Trademark Act for services or materials furnished by the Office, subject to the limitation that fees may be set/adjusted only to recover the aggregate estimated costs to the Office for processing, activities, services, and materials relating to patents (or trademarks), including administrative costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authority subject to statutory constraints (cost recovery) and to other procedural provisions in the Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public and advisory‑committee procedures for fee changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Before publishing a proposed fee, the Director must submit the proposed fee not less than 45 days prior to publication to the appropriate Patent/Trademark Public Advisory Committee(s). The committee(s) get a 30‑day period to deliberate, consider, comment, and must hold a public hearing during that period. The committee must make available a written report of comments and recommendations. The Director must consider committee input before setting/adjusting fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When publishing a proposed fee in the Federal Register the Director must include specific rationale/purpose, notify Chair and Ranking Members of Judiciary Committees, provide a public comment period of not less than 45 days, publish the final rule in the Federal Register and the PTO Official Gazette, and the fee may not become effective before the 45‑day congressional comment period or if a law disapproves the fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule of construction regarding applicant and treaty rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules prescribed under the fee‑setting section shall not diminish the rights of an applicant for a patent under title 35 or for a mark under the Trademark Act, nor any rights under a ratified treaty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects substantive applicant and treaty rights from being reduced by fee rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retention and sunset of fee‑setting authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director retains authority to set or adjust fees under the subsection only while the Patent and Trademark Office remains an agency within the Department of Commerce. Separately, the authority to set or adjust any fee under the provision shall terminate upon expiration of the 7‑year period beginning on the enactment date (subject to exceptions for regulations issued before termination).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior regulations and pending rulemakings are not affected by the termination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee reductions for small entities and micro entities
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees for filing, searching, examining, issuing, appealing, and maintaining patent applications/patents shall be reduced by 50% for entities qualifying as small entities and by 75% for micro entities (where specified). Subsection (h) further provides 50% reductions to small businesses, independent inventors, and nonprofit organizations for many fees; and additional 75% reduction for electronic filing for entities qualifying under paragraph (1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain surcharges/fees shall not be higher for small entities than for other entities in similar circumstances; the Director may provide regulations for implementation and refunds where prescribed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Micro entity — qualifying criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'micro entity' means an applicant who certifies that the applicant: (1) qualifies as a small entity under regulations; (2) has not been named as an inventor on more than 4 previously filed patent applications (with exclusions for foreign, provisional, and certain international applications); (3) in the preceding calendar year had gross income not exceeding 3 times the median household income (as reported by the Census); and (4) has not assigned, granted, or conveyed, nor is under obligation to assign, a license or ownership interest to an entity whose gross income in the preceding calendar year exceeded 3 times median household income.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions: applications resulting from prior employment where applicant assigned rights as a result of prior employment are not counted under (2); foreign currency incomes use average IRS exchange rate; institutions of higher education may qualify under specified conditions; the Director may impose additional limits (with at least 3 months' prior notice to Judiciary Committees).

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic filing incentive / surcharge for non‑electronic filings
rubrics_metrics.description: An additional fee of $400 is established for each application for an original patent (except design, plant, or provisional) that is not filed by electronic means as prescribed by the Director. The fee is reduced by 50% for small entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All fees paid under this subsection shall be deposited in the Treasury as an offsetting receipt that shall not be available for obligation or expenditure; effective 60 days after enactment (unless otherwise specified).

rubrics_metrics.name: General patent service fee schedule (filing, size, excess claim fees, disclaimers, appeals, revival, extensions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Statutory fee amounts include: filing/basic national fees (e.g., $330 for original utility non‑provisional; $220 for design, plant, provisional; $330 for reissue; $330 basic national for PCT national stage); size fee: $270 for each additional 50 sheets (or equivalent) over 100 sheets; excess claims fees: $220 for each independent claim in excess of 3, $52 per claim in excess of 20, $390 for each multiple dependent claim; disclaimer fee $140; appeal fees: $540 to file appeal to PTAB, $540 for filing brief, $1,080 to request oral hearing; revival fees $1,620 (reduced to $540 in some enumerated petitions); extension‑of‑time petition fees: $130 (first), $360 (second), $620 (third+).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director may by regulation provide refunds for canceled claims before examination and rectify errors in payment per prescribed regulations; many fees are subject to small/micro entity reductions as specified elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination and issue fees schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: Examination fees statutory amounts: $220 for examination of each original utility/plant (varies: $220 utility, $140 design, $170 plant; $220 for national stage; $650 for reissue examination). Issue fees: $1,510 for original utility (except design/plant), $860 design, $1,190 plant, $1,510 reissue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicability provisions tie these fees to other statutory payment provisions (e.g., section 111(a) and 371(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance fees and grace period
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintenance fees for patents (filed on or after Dec 12, 1980): 3.5 years after grant $980; 7.5 years after grant $2,480; 11.5 years after grant $4,110. Unless payment is received on/before due date or within a 6‑month grace period thereafter, the patent shall expire at the end of the grace period. The Director may require payment of a surcharge as a condition of accepting payment within the 6‑month grace period. No maintenance fee may be established for design or plant patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subsection allows grace period surcharge and notes expiration if not paid within the period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent search fees and other miscellaneous fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Search fees (adjusted to recover estimated average search cost): example statutory amounts include $540 for each original utility application (excl provisional/design/plant), $100 for design, $330 for plant, $540 for national stage, $540 for reissue. Other fees to be established to recover costs, but statutory listed fees include: recording a document affecting title $40 per property; photocopy $.25 per page; black and white copy of a patent $3; yearly fee for providing a library uncertified printed copies $50.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director may provide refunds for search fees upon express abandonment before examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees for small entities and electronic filing reduction specifics
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to paragraph (3), fees charged under subsections (a), (b), and (d)(1) shall be reduced by 50% for qualifying small entities (as defined) and for independent inventors or nonprofit organizations per regulations. For entities to which the small entity reduction applies, the filing fee under subsection (a)(1)(A) shall be reduced by 75% if the application is filed electronically as prescribed by the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Surcharges and other fees for small entities shall not exceed those required of other entities under similar circumstances; regulations will implement details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritized examination (track) — fee and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: A prioritized examination fee of $4,800 is established for filing a request for prioritized examination of a nonprovisional utility or plant application. In addition to this fee, the normal filing, search, examination (including applicable excess claims and application size fees), processing fee, and publication fee are due.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director may prescribe conditions and limits by regulation. Until regulations are prescribed, no prioritized application may contain/amend to more than 4 independent claims or more than 30 total claims. The Director may not accept more than 10,000 prioritization requests in any fiscal year until regulations set another limit.
